name: Odual
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Comson, E. 1987. The phonology of Odual; also Kari, E. E. 2009. A grammatical description of the Odual language (both cited in Wikipedia 'Odual language'; not online).

sources.note: No phonology; only that Odual differs from Abua in 'intonation, with the Oduals having a more rising intonation'. Works-cited list matches Glottolog plus Kari 2011 orthography and Kari 2007a.

sources.citation: Kari, Ethelbert Emmanuel. 2017. Central Delta languages: An overview. Stellenbosch Papers in Linguistics 47: 1-26. DOI 10.5774/47-0-213.
sources.note: Sec. 3 'Phonological overview' (vowels, consonants, syllable/morpheme structure, tone). Sec. 3.4 Tone, p. 11: 'all Central Delta lects operate a basic two-tone system' (quoting Alex 1989:24), L and H plus downstep, tone anchored on vowels and syllabic nasals; Odual minimal tone pairs from Kari 2009: 9, 12 (ózú 'to pour' / òzú 'skin'); tone distinguishes statement vs question in Odual (Kari 2009:12). No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the 26 pages.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2008. The Central Delta languages: Comparative word list and historical reconstructions. Cambridge: ms., 46 pp. (the Internet Archive 2015-04-21 copy of rogerblench.info; live domain hijacked).
sources.note: Comparative wordlist with reconstructions; only prosodic remark is that Wolff's (1969) 'notations of tone and vowel quality appear to be' unreliable (p. 2 area, the text). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Kari, Ethelbert E. 2007. The pronominal system of Oḍual. Studies in African Linguistics 36(1): 91-113. DOI 10.32473/sal.v36i1.107306.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sec. 2 gives the 20-vowel system (10 single + 10 double vowels, ATR harmony; double vowels = one syllable of two moras) and fn. 5 (p. 94) states 'two basic tones in Odual, low and high, plus a downstep'; tone patterns of every pronoun are described. Data from the Adibaam dialect; Comson 1987 named as the detailed phonology.

sources.citation: Kari, Ethelbert Emmanuel. 2009. A grammatical description of the Oḍual language. Minoh: Research Institute for World Languages, Osaka University (LiCCOSEC v. 5, ISSN 1883-0633). xvii+100 pp.

sources.note: The only full description of Odual; Kari 2017 cites its pp. 9 and 12 for the tone system, so its phonology chapter is where any statement on stress/accent would sit. Held by 17 Japanese libraries (CiNii NCID BA90093589; NDL bib 10280809); not in OUKA.
